purpose: Bounded TR10-1 VCO/DCDC characterization using recovered OpenRule1um source artifacts, measured VCO clock points, and an explicit TR-1um device-name/model conversion.

legacy_device_mapping.geometry_policy: Preserve W/L from the recovered source deck

evaluation_modes.name: openrule1um_source
evaluation_modes.meaning: Historical source-level reference using the original nchor1ex/pchor1ex models

evaluation_modes.name: tr1um_mapped
evaluation_modes.meaning: Engineering conversion using current TR-1um NMOS/PMOS wrappers; not foundry-qualified PDK migration

source_topology.older_slide_conflict: slide2.png shows a diode and 10-ohm load resistor, but the checked-in dcdc_down_full_tb source/netlist contains no diode instance; neither was silently added.

metrics: efficiency when delivered input power is positive

integrated_openrule1um_source_vctrl_5V.interpretation: The recovered legacy integrated source runs, but its simulated VCO is approximately 1.606 MHz at VCTRL=5 V, not the 33.736669 kHz silicon measurement; use external-clock rows for DCDC separation.

external_clock_at_measured_5V.interpretation: At the measured 33.736669 kHz clock, both model sets produce approximately 3.06–3.15 V into 10 kOhm and approximately 3.35–3.51 V into 1 MOhm; the converted TR-1um model is an engineering comparison, not a silicon match.

frequency_and_load_boundary: At 1.652357852 Hz, Vout is effectively zero through 1 MOhm; only the 1 GOhm case charges to approximately 0.34–0.38 V and is not a useful loaded operating point.
At 20.17090997 kHz, 10–10 kOhm loads remain in discontinuous/high-ripple operation; 1 MOhm reaches approximately 2.75–2.89 V.
At 33.736669 kHz, 10 kOhm and lighter loads reach approximately 3.06–3.15 V, while 10-ohm loading collapses to approximately 0.37–0.48 V.
At 90 kHz, the exact source topology reaches approximately 3.30–3.46 V into 1 MOhm, but remains below approximately 1.72 V into 10 kOhm.
key_results.model_conversion_delta: The TR-1um mapped rows differ materially from the OpenRule1um reference, generally increasing Vout at the measured clock points; this is expected from model/PDK conversion uncertainty and is not evidence of a foundry-equivalent migration.

current_tr1um_vco_reference.comparability_note: This converted/RCX VCO reference is not a calibrated reproduction of the 33.736669 kHz TR10-1 silicon point and must not be used to infer the DCDC VCO's silicon parameters.

limitations: The recovered DCDC source uses the legacy OpenRule1um PDK; the TR-1um rows are explicit device-name/model substitution only.
No foundry-qualified analog LVS, RCX, or silicon-calibrated compact-model migration was available for OpenRule1um to TR-1um.
The DCDC sweep injects measured/external clock waveforms; it does not calibrate or validate the VCO model.
No package, bondwire, board parasitic, oscilloscope probe, ESR, or inductor DCR model is included.
The source/netlist has no diode instance despite an older slide image showing one; that topology conflict remains unresolved.
A positive efficiency is not reported when the simulated source current indicates net power delivery back into the input source.
